faq.q: What is the origin of Hanieh?
faq.a: Hanieh is associated with Arabic. Hanieh is Arabic هَانِيَة (Hāniya), a feminine form associated with the sense 'happy, content'.
Yes — the underlying form هَانِيَة is Arabic.
Hanieh can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Hanieh should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Hāniya is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: In Persian, Hanieh is rendered هانیه and carries the sense هانیه، شاد.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Hanieh, hanieh. Script forms are هانيه, هانیه, هَانِيَة, ہانیہ, हानिया.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
